sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp.
sources.note: Sepen entry (sec. 2.23.12.12, pp. 143-144) is the first identification of the language: villages Akukum and Sepen, 'The language has not been recorded previously', lexical percentages only (Sepen-Mikarew 60%, Sepen-Giri 60%); Misegian typology (p. 145) lists phonemes only. General remark p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' — applies to all languages in the study; nothing Sepen-specific.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid sepe1240 (page and JSON), and Wikipedia 'Akukem language'.
sources.note: Glottolog references: Z'graggen 1969/1972/1974 (all 'wordlist_or_less'), Laycock 1973, ISO CR, Ethnologue; no descriptive source; Foley 2018 cited only for subclassification. Wikipedia is a stub citing Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa. Language Science Press (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 372), ch. 1 (LaTeX source and bibliography).
sources.note: Lists Akukem (spm, sepe1240) only in the Ramu family tree and name table; cites no source for it. Nothing on Sepen phonology.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-023 [spm] (submitted by Martha L. Wade, Pioneer Bible Translators PNG; supporter Mike Herchenroeder; adopted 2012-02-03).
sources.note: Adds the name Akukem / Akɨghɨm at the speakers' request (2006); no linguistic description, no sources cited beyond first-hand knowledge.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (n.d., data 2 Oct 2010 from Don R. Daniels, UCSB). Numeral systems of the world's languages: Sepen (Akukem).
sources.note: Six numerals in IPA (uvʰuavɨra 'one', pʰunĩ:ni 'two'...) with no stress marks; Daniels notes speakers prefer the name Akukem. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. 156 pp.
sources.note: Sepen = L7 (villages Akukum 137, Sepen 1 189, Sepen 2 102; total 428); source index p. 137 gives only 'WS' (Wurm 1971, names/classification). No linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 148 SEPEN (pop. 409; villages Akukum, Sepen No. 1, Sepen No. 2): 'All data, except population, from Z'graggen (1971)'. No phonology; the word 'stress' does not occur in the volume.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Published version of the thesis; Sepen sec. 2.23.12.12 (p. 77) repeats the identification paragraph; no phonology and no stress statement for Sepen.
